basic.expert_explanation: 80-100Hz: This is the standard rumble zone (AC hum, footsteps). Cutting here cleans up the mix headroom significantly.

expert_quote.text: Low end space is expensive. Don't waste it on non-bass instruments.
expert_quote.author: Spectrum Management

basic.title: Question 7
basic.content: The fader controls:
basic.expert_explanation: Fader: The final volume control for the mix. It's logarithmic, offering fine-tuned control around the 'Unity' (0dB) mark.

expert_quote.text: Mixing is balancing relative levels. The fader is your primary tool.
expert_quote.author: Mixing 101

basic.title: Question 8
basic.content: Unity gain on a fader is:
basic.expert_explanation: Unity (0): The point on the fader where the signal puts out exactly what it takes in. No boost, no cut. The 'neutral' position.

expert_quote.text: Start your mix with faders at unity and use gain to balance.
expert_quote.author: Pro Workflow

basic.title: Question 9
basic.content: Pan control positions sound:

answers.text: Left to right in stereo field

basic.expert_explanation: Pan (Panorama): Moves signal Left or Right. Using Pan creates a 'soundstage', allowing listeners to visualize where musicians are standing.

expert_quote.text: LCR (Left-Center-Right) is the secret to wide, clear mixes.
expert_quote.author: Panning Strategy

basic.title: Question 10
basic.content: Solo button allows you to:
basic.expert_explanation: Solo (SIP): Solos the track IN PLACE (with panning/FX). Great for critical listening. Beware: PFL Solo monitors the raw input signal instead.

expert_quote.text: Solo is for technical checking. Mixing happens in context.
expert_quote.author: Warning

intermediate.title: Question 1
intermediate.content: Signal flow order in channel strip is:

answers.text: Input → HPF → EQ → Dynamics → Fader → Pan

intermediate.expert_explanation: VCA Fader: Voltage Controlled Amplifier. A remote control fader. It changes the volume of other faders without audio actually passing through it.

expert_quote.text: Panning is fundamentally about creating space and room in between sounds.
expert_quote.author: Mixing Philosophy

intermediate.title: Question 2
intermediate.content: High-pass filter before EQ allows:

answers.text: Removing rumble before EQ processes signal

intermediate.expert_explanation: Pan Law: Does the sound get louder when you pan center? A -3dB Pan Law dips the volume in the center to maintain perceived constant loudness.

expert_quote.text: My job has very little to do with music. It has more to do with taste and culture and balance.
expert_quote.author: Rick Rubin

intermediate.title: Question 3
intermediate.content: Insert effects process signal:
intermediate.expert_explanation: Matrix Mix: A mixer within a mixer. Taking the Group Outputs (Drums, Vocals) and creating alternate mixes (Livestream, Foyer, Record).

expert_quote.text: Pay attention to the details here; they make the difference.
expert_quote.author: Study Guide

intermediate.title: Question 4
intermediate.content: Post-fader send means send level:
intermediate.expert_explanation: Direct Out: Taking the clean signal right after the preamp, bypassing the rest of the console. Used for recording live shows to a multitrack.

expert_quote.text: Every great producer understands these fundamentals.
expert_quote.author: Industry Standard

intermediate.title: Question 5
intermediate.content: Pre-fader send is used for:
intermediate.expert_explanation: Solo Safe: A mode that prevents a channel (like an FX Return) from being muted when you solo another channel. Keeps the reverb heard.

expert_quote.text: This topic connects directly to better mixing and recording.
expert_quote.author: Course Notes

intermediate.title: Question 6
intermediate.content: Unity gain on fader (+0dB) means:
intermediate.expert_explanation: Inline Console: A complex desk where the Input path (Mic) and Monitor path (Tape Return) share the SAME channel strip. Confusion for beginners.

expert_quote.text: Don't just memorize terms. Understand the physics.
expert_quote.author: Deep Learning

intermediate.title: Question 7
intermediate.content: Pan law of -3dB means:

answers.text: Center position is -3dB vs hard L/R

intermediate.expert_explanation: Flip Button: Swapping the small fader and large fader on an inline console. Commonly used to mix with the big faders.

expert_quote.text: Using faders allows you to learn and interact with your mix, pushing stuff up and hearing what it moves.
expert_quote.author: Pro Mixing Tip

intermediate.title: Question 8
intermediate.content: Aux send at 0dB sends what amount?
intermediate.expert_explanation: Unity Gain Architecture: Setting every fader to 0 and adjusting input gains so the mix is balanced 'flat'. A good starting point for clarity.

expert_quote.text: Panning is fundamentally about creating space and room in between sounds.
expert_quote.author: Mixing Philosophy

intermediate.title: Question 9
intermediate.content: Phase invert button is placed:
intermediate.expert_explanation: Automation Mode: Read, Write, Touch, Latch. 'Latch' stays where you leave it. 'Touch' snaps back when you let go. Critical for mixing.

expert_quote.text: If you know what you want to do and you do it, that's the work of a craftsman. If you begin with a question and use it to guide an adventure of discovery, that's the work of the artist.
expert_quote.author: Rick Rubin

intermediate.title: Question 10
intermediate.content: Phantom power switch typically affects:
intermediate.expert_explanation: Talkback Dim: When you press the Talkback button, the control room speakers automatically dim (-20dB) to prevent feedback loops.

expert_quote.text: Pay attention to the details here; they make the difference.
expert_quote.author: Study Guide

basic.title: Question 1
basic.content: Digital clipping occurs when:
basic.expert_explanation: Clipping Risk: Digital clipping is unforgiving. It sounds like static. Unlike analog tape, there is no 'good' digital distortion.

expert_quote.text: Pay attention to the details here; they make the difference.
expert_quote.author: Study Guide

basic.title: Question 2
basic.content: Digital clipping sounds:
basic.expert_explanation: Headroom: Think of it as 'ceiling height'. You don't build a house with a 6ft ceiling; you build 9ft so you can jump without hitting your head.

expert_quote.text: Every great producer understands these fundamentals.
expert_quote.author: Industry Standard

basic.title: Question 3
basic.content: Can you fix digital clipping after recording?
basic.expert_explanation: Yellow is Good: In modern digital meters, green is quiet, yellow is healthy (-18 to -6), and red is dangerous. Stay in the yellow.

expert_quote.text: This topic connects directly to better mixing and recording.
expert_quote.author: Course Notes

basic.title: Question 4
basic.content: Red clip indicators mean:
basic.expert_explanation: Soft Clip: A feature on some limiters that rounds off the corners of the wave instead of chopping them flat. Sounds warmer and less harsh.

expert_quote.text: Don't just memorize terms. Understand the physics.
expert_quote.author: Deep Learning

basic.title: Question 5
basic.content: Leaving 6dB headroom means peaks are at:
basic.expert_explanation: Master Bus Creep: You push the drum fader, then the bass, then the vocal. Suddenly the master is clipping. Turn everything DOWN instead.

expert_quote.text: I wanted to use the studio like a microscope for sound, which is what good engineers do.
expert_quote.author: Brian Eno

basic.title: Question 6
basic.content: Why leave headroom?
basic.expert_explanation: Visual Waveform: If your recorded waveform looks like a solid block with flat tops, it is clipped. You cannot fix this. Re-record it.

expert_quote.text: Pay attention to the details here; they make the difference.
expert_quote.author: Study Guide

basic.title: Question 7
basic.content: Recording at -18dBFS average provides:
basic.expert_explanation: Bit Depth Safety: 24-bit recording gives you a massive noise floor safety net. You can record quietly to avoid clipping and turn it up later safely.

expert_quote.text: Every great producer understands these fundamentals.
expert_quote.author: Industry Standard

basic.title: Question 8
basic.content: If you see red clipping lights:
basic.expert_explanation: Limiter on Output: A safety belt. Always have a limiter set to -0.1dB on your output when bouncing files to ensure no stray peaks ruin the file.

expert_quote.text: This topic connects directly to better mixing and recording.
expert_quote.author: Course Notes

basic.expert_explanation: Subtractive EQ is the practice of cutting unwanted frequencies (mud, resonance, hiss) rather than boosting good ones. This preserves headroom and often sounds more natural.

expert_quote.text: It's better to cut the mud than to boost the clarity.

intermediate.title: Question 1
intermediate.content: Why does the maxim "cut to fix, boost to enhance" exist?
intermediate.expert_explanation: Masking is best resolved with subtractive EQ. If the kick and bass clash at 80Hz, cutting 80Hz from the bass (or sidechaining) makes the kick punch through without simply turning the kick up.

expert_quote.text: Carving space is how you make a mix sound huge.
expert_quote.author: Chris Lord-Alge

basic.title: Question 1
basic.content: What does "additive EQ" mean?
basic.expert_explanation: Additive EQ involves boosting frequencies to enhance character. 'Air' describes frequencies above 10kHz that add sheen. 'Presence' is typically 3-6kHz. 'Thump' is 60-100Hz.

explanation_image.alt: Chart: Air, Body, Thump, Presence ranges

expert_quote.text: Boost wide for tone, cut narrow for problems.
expert_quote.author: EQ Golden Rule

expert_quote.text: Contrast creates width. If everything is wide, nothing is wide.

basic.title: Question 1
basic.content: What is headroom in mastering context?
basic.expert_explanation: Headroom is the space between your highest peak level and 0dBFS (clipping). Leaving 3-6dB of headroom allows the mastering engineer to apply EQ and compression without immediately hitting the digital ceiling.

expert_quote.text: Louder isn't better. Better is better.

basic.title: Question 1
basic.content: What does a limiter do?
basic.expert_explanation: A Limiter is a compressor with a ratio of infinity:1 and a very fast attack. It prevents signal from exceeding a specific ceiling (e.g., -1.0 dBTP) while raising the overall loudness of the track.

expert_quote.text: The ceiling is the Law. The threshold is the volume.
expert_quote.author: Limiter Physics
